previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, kidney transplant, chronic heart failure, complete heart block, and prior infections was readmitted one day after discharge due to bleeding and pain at the abdominal incision site following explant of a pacemaker generator. He had recently undergone placement of a Micra leadless pacemaker and removal of the abdominal device. Examination revealed a hematoma at the incision site, likely aggravated by coughing and hiccups. He underwent successful evacuation of the hematoma and cauterization of the bleeding source. His postoperative course was stable, with controlled pain, no further bleeding, and resumption of aspirin. He continued all baseline medications, including immunosuppressants, heart failure, and diabetes therapies. He was discharged home with a pressure dressing, a one-week course of cephalexin, activity restrictions, and follow-up in the device clinic.

upstroke and continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic velocity
of 43 cm/sec.  Vascularity is symmetric throughout this transplant.  The
transplant renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

Renal transplant labeled #2 is in the more medial and inferior position in the
right lower quadrant.  The transplant renal morphology of #2 is normal.
Specifically, the cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity, pyramids are
normal, there is no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal. 
There is no hydronephrosis.

For kidney #2 the resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.70 to

centimeters/second.  Vascularity is symmetric throughout this transplant.  The
transplant renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

IMPRESSION:



1. Resolved hydronephrosis in transplant kidney #1, the more superolateral
kidney.
2. Elevated peak systolic flow is noted in the main renal artery of transplant
kidney #2,  the more inferior medial kidney.  This could be further evaluated
with CT or MRI or short-term follow-up ultrasound could be performed to assess
stability.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  CT or MRI could be performed to evaluate elevated peak
systolic flow in the medial inferior renal transplant or a short-term
follow-up ultrasound could be obtained to assess stability.
